DGV runs a per-joint step input and measures overshoot, settling
time, and oscillation count. It needs at least one joint that has
BOTH (i) UsdPhysicsDriveAPI applied with positive stiffness, and
(ii) authored joint limits with non-zero range. Without that, the
controller has nothing to drive.

FIX (most common cause: missing PhysicsDriveAPI). On each actuated
revolute joint, apply DriveAPI and author stiffness / damping /
maxForce. Edit the prim in your USD file:

    def PhysicsRevoluteJoint "shoulder_pan_joint" (
        prepend apiSchemas = ["PhysicsDriveAPI:angular"]
    )
    {
        rel physics:body0 = </Base>
        rel physics:body1 = </ShoulderLink>
        uniform token physics:axis = "Z"

        # Joint limits (REQUIRED -- DGV skips joints with zero range)
        float physics:lowerLimit = -180.0
        float physics:upperLimit =  180.0

        # Drive gains. Tune per-joint -- heavier proximal links
        # need higher stiffness/damping than distal wrists.
        # Starting envelope (DJ.006): stiffness ~100-10000,
        # damping ~1-100; the UR10 reference asset uses values
        # from ~7 (wrist 3) up to ~360000 (shoulder lift).
        float drive:angular:physics:stiffness = 1000.0
        float drive:angular:physics:damping   = 50.0
        float drive:angular:physics:maxForce  = 1000.0
        float drive:angular:physics:targetPosition = 0.0
    }

For PRISMATIC joints use drive:linear:* (same scheme). For mimic
followers leave drive stiffness/damping at 0.0 -- they get their
position from the reference joint via PhysxMimicJointAPI and are
EXPECTED to be excluded from DGV.

     genuinely correct but the defaults are wrong for it):
     - Reduce `target_radius_factors` (default (0.5, 0.7, 0.9))

MIM: no PhysxMimicJointAPI found on any joint under the asset prim.

  Found:    0 joints with PhysxMimicJointAPI applied
  Expected: at least one revolute or prismatic joint with
            PhysxMimicJointAPI:<axisToken> applied (rotX/rotY/rotZ
            or transX/transY/transZ)

FIX (if your asset has coupled joints, e.g. a parallel-jaw gripper
where the two finger joints must move together):
  1. Pick the driven joint and call it the REFERENCE joint. Leave
     it with a normal drive (PhysicsDriveAPI or JointStateAPI).
  2. On each FOLLOWER joint, apply PhysxMimicJointAPI keyed to that
     joint's physics:axis instance token (e.g. "rotX" for a
     revolute joint with physics:axis = "X").
  3. Set physxMimicJoint:<axis>:gearing (non-zero) and
     physxMimicJoint:<axis>:referenceJoint pointing at the
     reference joint's prim path.
  4. Both follower AND reference joints must have physics:lowerLimit
     and physics:upperLimit authored, and neither may have
     physics:excludeFromArticulation = true.

Paste-ready USDA snippet (adapt paths, axis token, gearing sign,
and limits to your asset):

    # The follower joint: applies PhysxMimicJointAPI keyed to the axis
    # token of the joint (rotX/rotY/rotZ for revolute, transX/transY/
    # transZ for prismatic). The instance name MUST match physics:axis.
    def PhysicsRevoluteJoint "follower_joint" (
        prepend apiSchemas = ["PhysxMimicJointAPI:rotX"]
    )
    {
        uniform token physics:axis = "X"
        rel physics:body0 = <./path/to/parent_link>
        rel physics:body1 = <./path/to/follower_link>
        float physics:lowerLimit = -45.0   # required: limits must be authored
        float physics:upperLimit =  45.0

        # ---- PhysxMimicJointAPI:rotX attributes ----
        # gearing: Δq_follower = gearing * Δq_reference + offset
        # Must be a non-zero real number. Sign encodes direction:
        # -1 = follower moves opposite the reference (typical for
        # parallel-jaw grippers where one jaw mirrors the other).
        float physxMimicJoint:rotX:gearing = -1.0
        float physxMimicJoint:rotX:offset = 0.0
        float physxMimicJoint:rotX:naturalFrequency = 100.0
        float physxMimicJoint:rotX:dampingRatio = 0.0
        # referenceJoint must point at a joint that does NOT itself
        # carry PhysxMimicJointAPI (no chains/cycles).
        rel physxMimicJoint:rotX:referenceJoint = <./path/to/reference_joint>
    }

  - Articulation DOFs reported by Isaac: 12
  - DOFs with finite (lower, upper) and upper-lower > 1e-6: 0
  - Required by MJC: >= 2 (each driven independently to a mid-range

        float physics:lowerLimit = 0.0      # meters
        float physics:upperLimit = 0.085    # meters
        # ... body0 / body1 / localPos0 / localPos1 ...

  - physics:axis is set (X / Y / Z).

results.message: Slope drop FAILED: The asset remained too far from the ramp after contact for 24 consecutive frame(s); peak clearance 0.3401m at frame 457. Review collision contact gaps, restitution, and the video for an upward launch.

STA: 4/12 joints failed state accuracy.

FAILING JOINTS: FL_Knee_joint, FR_Knee_joint, HL_Knee_joint, HR_Knee_joint

WHAT WE FOUND:
  At least one joint could not hold its commanded position within
  the tolerance during the 5-waypoint test. Per-joint detail (max
  position error in degrees, failed targets) is in the warnings
  above and recorded as `sta_max_position_error_deg` in
  result.json.

FIX (in priority order):
  1. Raise drive stiffness/damping on the failing joint(s). On
     each joint prim, edit:
         float drive:angular:physics:stiffness = <larger value>
         float drive:angular:physics:damping   = <larger value>
     For ARM/SCARA robots FET022 disables robot gravity per-body
     during STA, so the drive only needs to overcome link inertia;
     a few hundred N-m/rad is usually enough. If you see large
     steady-state errors specifically on horizontal-axis joints,
     the per-body gravity disable may have failed -- check the
     `articulation.disable_gravity()` and `per-body
     disable_gravity` events from RobotHandle.initialize in the
     log.
  2. If the joint oscillates instead of settling, raise damping
     by 2-5x before raising stiffness further.
  3. Verify authored position limits include the test waypoints.
     The test commands joints to small +/-step targets around 0
     by default; if 0 is outside your authored range, the test
     cannot reach it. Edit `physics:lowerLimit` /
     `physics:upperLimit` on the joint prim.
  4. Inspect downstream mass. A heavy distal link causes upstream
     joints to undershoot under default gains. Re-check
     `physxRigidBody:mass` and `physxRigidBody:diagonalInertia`
     on each downstream link.
  5. Increase `test_duration_seconds` (default 3.0) only if the
     joint is slow but does reach the target eventually.
  6. Loosen `position_tolerance_deg` (default 5.0) only when
     intentional steady-state error is acceptable for the asset.

STA cannot run: no testable joints after filtering.

WHAT WE FOUND:
  - passive joints (no UsdPhysics:DriveAPI authored): 12
      FL_HipX_joint, FL_HipY_joint, FL_Knee_joint, FR_HipX_joint, FR_HipY_joint, FR_Knee_joint, HL_HipX_joint, HL_HipY_joint, HL_Knee_joint, HR_HipX_joint, HR_HipY_joint, HR_Knee_joint
  - mimic-follower joints (PhysxMimicJointAPI -> reference): 0
      (none)
  - articulated joints with finite, non-degenerate limits and a
    drive authored: 0

WHAT WE EXPECTED:
  At least one revolute or prismatic joint with:
    1. finite lower/upper position limits where |hi - lo| >= 0.01 rad,
    2. UsdPhysics:DriveAPI applied (angular for revolute,
       linear for prismatic), and
    3. no PhysxMimicJointAPI making it a follower of another joint.

FIX: Apply DriveAPI on the joint(s) that should be actuated, with
non-zero stiffness and a reasonable target (typically 0 rad at
rest pose). On the joint prim in your USD, paste:

    over "<joint_prim_name>" (
        prepend apiSchemas = ["PhysicsDriveAPI:angular",
                              "PhysicsJointStateAPI:angular"]
    )
    {
        # Position-control drive. Stiffness in N-m/rad for angular,
        # N/m for linear. UR10 uses ~5,729,578 (1e8 deg/rad-ish);
        # most arms want 1e4 to 1e6 N-m/rad.
        float drive:angular:physics:stiffness = 100000.0
        float drive:angular:physics:damping   = 10000.0
        float drive:angular:physics:maxForce  = inf
        float drive:angular:physics:targetPosition = 0.0

        # Position limits in RADIANS for revolute, METERS for
        # prismatic. Must be finite and span the test waypoints
        # (default test commands +/-15 deg around 0).
        float physics:lowerLimit = -3.14159
        float physics:upperLimit =  3.14159

        # JointStateAPI -- required for STA to read back the
        # commanded position during the test.
        float state:angular:physics:position = 0.0
        float state:angular:physics:velocity = 0.0
    }

If a joint is INTENTIONALLY passive (e.g. a free-spinning caster),
tag it with `simready:joint:passive = true` so STA skips it without
counting it against the asset. If the asset is a pure-mimic
gripper (every DOF is a follower), STA does not apply -- mark the
reference joint with DriveAPI as above and let the followers be
driven by mimic.

results.message:
VEL: No joints carry an authored velocity limit; the velocity-limit test cannot run.

What the test looked for (EITHER authoring form is accepted):
  - `physxJoint:maxJointVelocity` on a PhysxJointAPI, OR
  - `physxDrivePerformanceEnvelope:angular:maxActuatorVelocity`
    (or `:linear:`) on a PhysxDrivePerformanceEnvelopeAPI,
  set to a positive finite value on each driven (revolute /
  prismatic) joint.
  - At least one such joint that is NOT a passive or mimic-
    follower joint (those are excluded -- their velocity is not
    independently commandable).

  UNITS: USD authors these in DEGREES/second for revolute joints
  and distance/second for prismatic joints. (PhysX consumes
  radians/second internally; the test converts deg->rad for you.)

What was found:
  - No joint carried either authored velocity limit, or every
    joint that did is passive / mimic-followed.

FIX: On every driven revolute/prismatic joint, author a positive
finite velocity limit matching the mechanism's datasheet rated
speed, in DEGREES/second (revolute) or distance/second
(prismatic).

Paste-ready USDA -- adjust the value to your joint's datasheet:

    def PhysicsRevoluteJoint "shoulder_pan_joint" (
        prepend apiSchemas = ["PhysicsDriveAPI:angular",
                              "PhysxJointAPI"]
    )
    {
        rel physics:body0 = </base_link>
        rel physics:body1 = </shoulder_link>
        uniform token physics:axis = "Z"
        # Rated max speed in DEGREES/s (UR10 shoulder = 120 deg/s
        # = ~2.09 rad/s).
        float physxJoint:maxJointVelocity = 120
    }

    def PhysicsPrismaticJoint "slide_joint" (
        prepend apiSchemas = ["PhysicsDriveAPI:linear",
                              "PhysxJointAPI"]
    )
    {
        rel physics:body0 = </base_link>
        rel physics:body1 = </slide_link>
        uniform token physics:axis = "X"
        # Rated max speed, distance/s.
        float physxJoint:maxJointVelocity = 1.0
    }

Notes:
  - The same limit can also (or instead) be authored on the
    actuator side as
    `physxDrivePerformanceEnvelope:angular:maxActuatorVelocity`
    (or `:linear:`), also in DEGREES/second for revolute; the
    test takes the MIN of the two when both are present, so
    author both consistently.
  - If every joint in the articulation is passive or a mimic
    follower, this phase has nothing to test -- add a velocity
    limit on the master joint that drives the followers.
